newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama posts new anti-drug police unit in jungle.
newsitem.headline: Panama posts new anti-drug police unit in jungle.

text.p: A new Panamanian police unit will begin duties on Monday in the remote Darien jungle along the Colombian border, long a haven for drug and weapons trafficking, said National Police Director Jose Sosa.

"We're concerned about drugs, guerrilla groups and the flood of illegal immigrants into Panama; that's why we're taking these measures," Sosa told reporters on Sunday during a tour of the training facilities in the small Darien cities of Yaviza and Meteti, some 30 miles (50 km) from Colombia's border and about 200 miles (320 km) from Panama City.

Called the Border Police Service, the 100-man unit will patrol the porous Colombian border with six helicopters donated from U.S. military reserves to locate traffickers and bring them to temporary holding cells in Meteti, Sosa said.

The unit is made up of officers from Panama's police, maritime, civilian air force and presidential secret police. Sosa said he hoped the unit would also dent the surging problem of illegal immigrants who have been flooding into Panama recently due to violent outbreaks in Colombia's northern provinces.
"Will 100 officers really make a difference? Put it this way, we didn't have anything before; we have to start with something," he said.
After an eight-week training course in jungle warfare, the unit will be based in Meteti, he said.
"They will have the authority to abide by all national police rules, including shooting if necessary, but we hope not to arrive to that ultimate consequence," he said.
"There are lots of problems of drugs and kidnappings," said Yaviza resident Carlos Palacio.

"Some unknown group recently kidnapped and killed a local businessman because the family didn't meet the ransom. I think these problems will drop now that the police will stay in the area," Palacio said.
